title: Standards ratchet on violation counts and a fresh review of large PRs before merge
body:
Source: operator 2026-11-19 marked Matt Pocock 'Watch me ship a 21,000-line feature with mattpocock/skills' (youtu.be/jVBlkOF8sHk, transcript in rss-news item 0e3384e12aa0) as very important; lead analysis mapped his loop onto KRN. Evidence: he splits review of a large diff across fresh Standards and Spec reviewer agents (each <=400 words) and turns every human review comment into a ratcheted lint whose violation count may only fall; KRN's Judge review is optional (repository-workflow.md) and standards checks are pass/fail with no ratchet for existing violations.
Files: src/ci/ship.ts, scripts/ratchet*.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml, test/ci/ratchet.test.ts
Outcome: a ratchet file records per-rule violation counts; CI fails when any count rises and lowers the recorded count when it falls, so a new standard can land without fixing every old instance; krn pr ship runs a fresh-context Standards+Spec review on a PR above a size threshold before auto-merge and posts findings as PR comments.
Proof: ratchet test: a raised count fails, a lowered count rewrites the file, an equal count passes; a ship test shows review ran above the threshold and not below.

Operator-forwarded weekly review, 2026-11-19, makes this more urgent. Measured over the last 300 merged PRs: 0 had any review. The median time from open to merge is 4.5 min, and the 36 PRs above 400 lines merged at a median of 5.1 min. Both guard gaps found this week (t-1kt1vb9, plus the /dev/fd bypass found by a fresh review before merge) were in code that CI does not test. Review src/hook and src/ci first. Constraints: Actions minutes stay free; Check stays the only required check; review must not move HEAD after a green Check (KRN-07). The pipeline audit is in .krn/runs/arch-review/pipeline.md.
